newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS: Chinese Mercantile issue out.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS: Chinese Mercantile issue out.

text.p: Chinese Mercantile Bank's US$20 million floating rate certificate of deposit (FRCD) issue, despite its small size, was the highlight of an otherwise quiet Asian debt market on Monday.
The three-year deal was launched into general syndication via arranger CS First Boston and Cho Hung Finance, and featured annual put and call options.
At an all-in of 150 basis points over London Interbank Offered Rate to an one-year put, bankers said the deal was seen as "very reasonable."
China's debt paper has regained its allure for investors, after the death of paramount leader Deng Xiao-ping in February cleared away uncertainty.
Also adding to China debt securities' attractions are the well publicised problems of the banking sectors of both South Korea and Thailand.
A banker said the Shenzhen-based bank's "impressive earning growth and strong parentage" would also bolster the issue.
Chinese Mercantile Bank's net profit has grown by 2.5 times, to US$8.67 million in 1996 from US$2.52 million in 1995.
The issuer is jointly-owned by Hong Kong Chinese Bank, China Travel Services Holdings Hongkong and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China.
While the paper is expected to attract a large syndicate, it might not do as well in secondary trade, a trader from a European bank commented.

An FRCD issued by Chinese Mercantile Bank last year has almost no liquidity, despite its credit quality. The issue paid 160 basis points over Singapore Interbank Offered Rate to top-tier for an effective tenor of one year.
"Banks seldom trade on one-year paper, they hold them to maturity", the trader explained.
Capitalising on improved sentiment on China, Guangdong Development Bank is expected to hit the debt market with a US$50 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue later this week.
The facility is expected to be for three years, including a a call option in year two, bankers said.
Pricing is rumored to be around 60 basis points. WestLB and Standard Chartered Bank are the arrangers, bankers said.
A new US$60 million loan facility for Fujian Enterprises Holding Co Ltd is also in the pipeline, bankers said.
Wholly owned by China's Fujian provincial government, the facility matures in five years and includes a put option in year four.

With an average life of 3.2 years, it is expected to pay an interest margin of 150 basis points over LIBOR, and fees are 100 basis points for co-arrangers, bankers said. -Angi Li Hong kong Newsroom (852) 2847 4039
